brief: JPMorgan Market Intelligence, afternoon of September 15, 2026. Stocks fell a second straight day into the FOMC decision, SPX -0.4%, NDX -0.6%, RTY -0.8%, with about 70% of SPX members lower. The desk attributes the pressure to oil rather than bonds. WTI rose 4.07% to $105.52 on a Saudi cargo cancellation, Libya outages and a Russian refinery cut, while 2y and 10y yields added under 1bp and the 10Y sits at 5.002%. Restaurants had their worst move since liberation day because crude keeps grinding higher and the 10-year holds above 5%, and with positioning at the 0th percentile the desk expects further multiple compression and lower re-rating. Into the Fed, 25bp is priced, 52bp for the year and 76bp by end-27Q1. Jay Barry sets out five outcomes without probabilities, judging no hike and crush inflation the least likely, and Mkt Intel maps each to an SPX move from -2% to +1%. Mkt Intel expects a less is more Warsh and two hikes rather than three, stays tactically cautious and neutral, argues bond volatility not yield levels is the equity headwind, and remains bullish Tech, Semis and Mag7 on improving AI monetization.
